(Baton Rouge, Louisiana) | college = [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2015–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | career_start = 2018 | years1 = [[2018–19 NBA G League season|2018]] | team1 = [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2018|full=y}} | team2 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years3 = [[2018–19 NBA G League season|2018–2019]] | team3 = →[[Windy City Bulls]] | years4 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019–2020]] | team4 = Rio Grande Valley Vipers | years5 = [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021]] | team5 = [[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years6 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team6 = [[Iowa Wolves]] | years7 = 2022 | team7 = [[Newfoundland Growlers (basketball)|Newfoundland Growlers]] | years8 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team8 = Iowa Wolves | years9 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team9 = [[Wisconsin Herd]] | years10 = 2023 | team10 = [[Hapoel Be'er Sheva B.C.|Hapoel Be'er Sheva]] | years11 = 2024 | team11 = [[Ottawa BlackJacks]] | years12 = 2025–present | team12 = [[Anhui Wenyi Basketball Club|Anhui Wenyi]] | highlights = * [[Louisiana Mr. Basketball]] (2015) }} '''Brandon Sampson''' (born May 1, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Anhui Wenyi Basketball Club|Anhui Wenyi]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU). ==High school career== Sampson was named [[Louisiana Mr. Basketball]] as a senior for [[Madison Preparatory Academy]] in 2015 after averaging 15.9 points, 2.9 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game in leading the team to a state championship.{{cite web|first=|last=|url=http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/-7024055653025786388/brandon-sampson-follows-in-jarell-martins-footsteps-named-lswa-mr-basketball/|title=Brandon Sampson follows in Jarell Martin's footsteps, named LSWA Mr. Basketball|work=[[The Times-Picayune]]|date=April 12, 2015|accessdate=January 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006193747/http://highschoolsports.nola.com/news/article/-7024055653025786388/brandon-sampson-follows-in-jarell-martins-footsteps-named-lswa-mr-basketball/|archive-date=October 6, 2015|url-status=dead}} He signed with coach [[Steve Lavin]] at [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]], but reopened his commitment when Lavin was fired in 2015. He ultimately signed with hometown [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]].{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Johnson|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/04/20/brandon-sampson-lsu-tigers-recruit-commit|title=LSU lands another star recruit, signing guard Brandon Sampson|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date= April 20, 2015|accessdate=January 1, 2019}} ==College career== Sampson was part of a heralded LSU recruiting class for coach [[Johnny Jones (basketball, born 1961)|Johnny Jones]], which also included future NBA players [[Ben Simmons]] and [[Antonio Blakeney]]. After a disappointing freshman season, which saw the Tigers underperform as a team and Sampson's minutes fluctuate, he found more consistency as a sophomore in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]].{{cite web|first=James|last=Bewers|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_879ba644-9d5d-11e6-b029-7b6d3426e893.html|title=With lessons learned from an inconsistent freshman year, LSU guard Brandon Sampson assumes a leadership role|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date= October 29, 2016|accessdate=January 1, 2019}} He averaged 11.6 points and 3.1 rebounds in 27.5 minutes per game, starting the majority of the season. As a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] the following year, Sampson suffered a severe ankle sprain, which caused him to miss a month of the season.{{cite web|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_d7ec151a-cfb2-11e7-ad4a-87dc24c0074a.html|title=LSU guard Brandon Sampson suffered severely sprained ankle, could be out a month|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date= November 22, 2017|accessdate=January 1, 2019}} Upon his return, Sampson had difficulty with consistency due to the lingering effects of the injury.{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Hickey|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/college/lsu-basketball-coach-will-wade-challenges-guard-brandon-sampson/QVB9ExnrPsZHjKLleEFG1N/|title=LSU basketball coach Will Wade challenges guard Brandon Sampson|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date= January 22, 2018|accessdate=January 1, 2019}} On the season, he averaged 7.7 points in 18.9 minutes per game. ==Professional career== Following his junior season, Sampson declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]], but was not selected. After playing for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Zac|last=Pacleb|title=After testing his luck, Ex-LSU guard Brandon Sampson's trying to make his mark in NBA Summer League|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_a9c57fea-855c-11e8-9bf9-67e003f9650f.html|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date= July 11, 2018|accessdate=January 1, 2019}} He then signed an exhibit 10 contract with the [[Houston Rockets]], who ultimately placed him on their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Feigen|title=Rockets sign Brandon Sampson to an Exhibit 10 contract|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-add-Brandon-Sampson-Angel-Rodriguez-to-G-13294434.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=October 9, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2019}} In 18 games with the Vipers, Sampson averaged 17.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. On December 27, 2018, Sampson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Under the terms of the agreement, he would split time with the Bulls' G League affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Brandon Sampson to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-brandon-sampson-two-way-contract|work=NBA.com|date= December 27, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2019}} He was assigned and made his Windy City debut the next night, scoring 17 points and passing for 5 assists in a win.{{cite web|title=Bulls Start Fast, Never Look Back In Win Over Blue|url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20181228/WCBOKL/|work=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2019}} Sampson later made his NBA debut on January 30, 2019, with 5 points and 2 rebounds recorded in a 105–89 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. On October 27, 2019, Sampson was included in the training camp roster of the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|title=VIPERS FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/vipers-finalize-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2019|access-date=October 27, 2019}} He had a season high 27 points on January 13, 2020, additionally posting five rebounds and two assists in a win over the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite news|title=Brandon Sampson: Posts season high in win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/brandon-sampson-posts-season-high-in-win/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=January 13, 2020|access-date=January 18, 2020}} In 42 games, Sampson averaged 13.2 points, 2.9 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game.{{cite news|first=Sonny|last=Shipp|title=Former LSU Tigers nearing a return to NBA action|url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/Former-LSU-Tigers-nearing-a-return-to-NBA-action-147530068/|work=247 Sports|date=May 26, 2020|access-date=May 31, 2020}} In 2020–21, Sampson played for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], appearing in 6 games in the pandemic-shortened season. On October 26, 2021, Sampson joined the [[Iowa Wolves]] after a trade.{{cite web|title=Iowa Wolves Announce Training Camp Roster and Finalize Coaching Staff|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-wolves-announce-training-camp-roster-and-finalize-coaching-staff/n-5758384|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} In 30 appearances, he averaged 14.4 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 2.0 assists.{{cite web|title=Growlers Sign Former Chicago Bulls Guard Brandon Sampson|url=https://www.cebl.ca/newfoundland-growlers-sign-former-chicago-bulls-guard-brandon-sampson|website=CEBL.ca|date=April 12, 2022|access-date=April 12, 2022}} On April 12, 2022, Sampson signed with the [[Newfoundland Growlers (basketball)|Newfoundland Growlers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League|CEBL]]. On November 2, 2022, Sampson was named to the opening night roster for the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-wolves-finalize-opening-night-roster/n-5895237|title=Iowa Wolves Finalize Opening Night
